newsitem.title: MALTA: Maltese Labour leader claims Euro poll victory.
newsitem.headline: Maltese Labour leader claims Euro poll victory.

text.p: Maltese Labour Party leader Alfred Sant claimed victory over the ruling Nationalists on Sunday after a general election campaign which committed the party to scrap the island's bid for European Union membership.
Sant, 48, said on radio: "There are clear indications that there is a Labour victory and I want to reaffirm our intention to form a government for all the people of Malta and Gozo."
There was no immediate statement from the Nationalist Party, led by Prime Minister Edward Fenech Adami.

Sant, who seeks a "special relationship" but not membership of the EU has also promised to pull Malta out of NATO's Partnership for Peace Programme which it joined last year. He wants the island to retain what he terms "positive neutrality".

Earlier on Sunday, a grim-faced Fenech Adami told reporters at the vote count centre: "The situation is still unclear. Predictions are subject of course to a margin of error which indeed could go either in favour of one party or the other."
He added: "It is going very definitely to be a very close finish."
His forecast contrasted with his party's record 13,000 vote majority at the last election in 1992 which gave it a three-seat majority in the 65-member parliament.
In the capital Valletta, Labour supporters hooted car horns and waved the party's red flags in anticipation.
Fenech Adami, who had confidently predicted Malta being ready for EU membership in mid-1988, promised a statement as soon as the result was certain.
